jurisdiction.venue: U.K. Competition and Markets Authority & European Commission (Case AT.40826)

headline: World’s Three Largest Fragrance Makers Fined €472 Million by EU and £85 Million by U.K. Over ‘Beer and Curry’ Cartel
deck: Givaudan, Firmenich, and IFF admitted four years of coordinating price hikes, energy surcharges, and a no-poach pact targeting Unilever via WhatsApp and London dinners—earning 20% to 65% leniency discounts and zero executive prosecutions.

score_provenance.rationale: Givaudan, Firmenich, and IFF admitted four years of EEA and U.K. fragrance collusion—receiving 20%–65% leniency discounts plus 10%–20% settlement cuts toward €471.97 million in EU fines and £85.17 million in U.K. fines (~$608 million combined across three multi-billion-dollar conglomerates)—with zero executives criminally charged or jailed.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: The European Commission fined Givaudan, Firmenich, and IFF €471.97 million and the U.K. CMA fined them £85.17 million (~$608M combined) after all three admitted four years of price coordination and no-poach collusion targeting Unilever, with zero executives charged.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Three regional grocery wholesalers meeting over dinner to rig shampoo and detergent prices for four years, confessing after a raid for a half-off coupon, and sending nobody to court
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Criminal price-fixing conspiracy charges in jurisdictions with individual cartel liability, versus pure corporate balance-sheet settlements here
